text:
mike: customer reports intermittent JSON framing errors when streaming with the Go SDK. error: "json: invalid character '\\n' in string literal" during streaming decode. happens after ~12–30s of a long response.

kevin: thanks — any chance they're on a specific Go SDK version? we've seen behavior change between v0.9.x and v0.11.x around chunk coalescing.

mike: they're on go-sdk v0.9.3. server side shows chunked responses with occasional zero-length chunk payloads (just "\\r\\n"). attaching truncated floor logs: 

```
> chunk: len=128 payload="{\"id\":\"r-...\", \"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"Hello\"}}]}\\r\\n"
> chunk: len=0 payload="\\r\\n"
> chunk: len=64 payload="{\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"world\"}}]}\\r\\n"
```

caroline: bufio.Scanner in stdlib chokes on tokens larger than MaxTokenSize, but zero-len chunks can also cause the scan loop to return unexpected tokens if boundary logic differs. is the SDK using Scanner or a stream-delimited JSON decoder?

kevin: Go SDK v0.9 used a custom scanner around bufio.Reader with ScanLines-like behavior to split on "\\r\\n" boundaries. v0.10 switched to a streaming JSON decoder that expects complete JSON objects per chunk. if an empty chunk arrives between two partial JSON fragments, the decoder can see an illegal sequence.

lauren: customer provided repro steps: make a long completion (>5k tokens) with slow token emission and artificially inject an empty chunk every ~20 chunks. They see either EOF on decoder or "invalid character '\\n'". repro script (simplified):

```
# server: simulate chunking
for i:=0;i<200;i++ {
  emitChunk(partialJson(i))
  if i%20==0 { emitChunk("") }
  time.Sleep(40*time.Millisecond)
}
```

mike: logs show client stuck in scan loop for ~9s then fails with json error. customer also mentions that upgrading to v0.11.0 on a branch fixed it for them.

kevin: v0.11 changed to a more permissive framing parser + coalescing: it merges adjacent non-empty chunks and ignores bare CRLF-only chunks. but that fix introduced a regression for some users relying on token boundaries for partial streaming (we discussed last month).

caroline: actionable steps: 1) confirm customer can upgrade to >=v0.11.0 and test; 2) if cannot, recommend a client-side workaround: use a Reader-based incremental JSON decoder instead of Scanner or increase max token buffer and ignore zero-len chunk tokens. Provide minimal patch snippet:

```
// workaround: skip empty chunks before decoding
for {
  chunk := readNextChunk(r)
  if len(chunk)==0 { continue }
  dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(chunk))
  var obj map[string]any
  if err := dec.Decode(&obj); err!=nil { log.Printf("decoding err: %v", err); continue }
  handle(obj)
}
```

lauren: also asked customer to capture raw bytes (hexdump) around the failure window and forward. that will tell us if there's an extra '\\n' or a stray '}' or truncation.

mike: customer says they can't move off v0.9.3 due to pinned CI deps. asked for backport patch.

kevin: ok I'll draft a tight backport: 1) explicitly ignore CRLF-only frames when splitting; 2) add a safety coalesce stage that will merge small subsequent chunks up to 512 bytes before feeding the decoder. will include toggles behind env var ENABLE_STREAM_COALESCE for minimal risk.

caroline: also raise an incident if we see >3 customer hits in a day. add metric: stream_decoder_errors_by_sdk_version.

mike: temporary mitigation to share with customer: set env REDWOOD_GO_STREAM_SPLIT=legacy (current) or coalesce to enable the new behavior. docs snippet: 

```
// env:
REDWOOD_GO_STREAM_SPLIT=coalesce
```

lauren: note for support ticket: repro steps, raw hexdump, SDK version, Go runtime version, and the exact model + max tokens. ticket updated.

mike: thanks everyone — kevin, please ping when you have the backport PR and I'll attach to the customer's case. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: deploy-batch-3 queued: runtime/stream-parser v0.11.1-backport -> staging (canary 1/3).
